333082.title: Concavity conjecture for polar-code interpolation functions
333082.statement:
For a prime-power alphabet size $q\geq2$, an integer kernel dimension $m\geq2$, and a parameter $\beta\in(0,1)$, define

$$
g_{0}(x)=(x(1-x))^{\beta}.
$$

**Concavity conjecture.** The function $\overline{g}_{n}(x)$ is concave on $[0,1]$ for every $n$.

If true, this would make the scaling analysis of the associated sequence of inhomogeneous polar codes rigorous in terms of $\lambda_m$. The source presents this as unproved; the notation $\overline{g}_n$ is not defined in the supplied span.

333117.title: Zhu's planar graph multiple list-colouring conjecture
333117.statement: A graph is $(k,m)$-choosable if, for every assignment of lists of $k$ colours to its vertices, it has a colouring in which each vertex receives $m$ colours from its list and adjacent vertices receive disjoint colour sets. **Zhu's conjecture.** There is a constant integer $m$ such that every planar graph $G$ is $(5m-1,m)$-choosable. This conjecture asks for a uniform multiple-list-colouring bound for planar graphs; the paper notes that the corresponding integer cannot be $1$, while its existence was posed as an open question.

333134.title: Multiple list-colouring conjecture for planar graphs at ratio $(9,2)$
333134.statement: A graph is **$(k,m)$-choosable** if, for every assignment of lists of at least $k$ colours to its vertices, it has an $m$-fold colouring in which each vertex receives $m$ colours from its list and adjacent vertices receive disjoint colour sets. **$(9,2)$-choosability conjecture.** Every planar graph is $(9,2)$-choosable. This is stronger than the preceding conjecture and would replace the known $1$-defective $(9,2)$-choosability result by the $0$-defective version, namely ordinary proper multiple list-colouring. The cited defective paintability result is due to Hladký and Zatloukal; whether the defect can be removed is open.

333144.title: Finite forbidden-subgraph characterization of hereditary equality of domination numbers
333144.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\gamma(G)$ and $\gamma_e(G)$ denote its domination number and exponential domination number, respectively. A graph is **hereditarily equal** when $\gamma(H)=\gamma_e(H)$ for every induced subgraph $H$ of it. **Finite forbidden-subgraph conjecture.** There is a finite set ${\cal F}$ of graphs such that a graph $G$ is hereditarily equal if and only if $G$ is ${\cal F}$-free. This conjecture seeks a finite characterization of graphs for which ordinary and exponential domination agree on every induced subgraph; the paper proposes it as part of its closing conjectures, with no resolution given here.

333240.title: Classification of orbits under curvature flow for homogeneous topological cloths
333240.statement: Let $\mathcal{G}^n$ be the class of embedded graphs in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Suppose $G\in\mathcal{G}^n$ is an embedded graph with a homogeneous topological cloth and a well-defined time evolution under curvature flow $G(t)$. **Classification of orbits conjecture.** Either $G(t)$ converges topologically to $\sigma_m$ for some $m\leq n$, or it converges to a stationary state. This conjecture predicts that homogeneous topological cloths have only universal or stationary long-time behavior; the source notes that it would not be surprising if $\sigma_n=\sigma_m$ for all $m,n\geq3$, but gives no resolution status.

333242.title: Xiong's stronger positivity conjecture for prime-indexed overpartition series
333242.statement:
Let $h(q)$ be the $q$-series

$$
h(q):=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n+1}q^{n(n+1)/2}}{1-q^n},
$$

let $(q)_\infty:=\prod_{n=1}^{\infty}(1-q^n)$, and let $p_1>p_2\geq 2$ be primes. **Xiong's stronger positivity conjecture.** The function

$$
\frac{p_1h(q^{p_1})-p_2h(q^{p_2})}{(q)_\infty}
$$

has positive coefficients of $q^n$ for every $n\geq p_2$, and nonnegative coefficients of $q^n$ for every $n\geq 1$. This stronger coefficientwise assertion is motivated by numerical evidence and, if true, implies the earlier positivity conjecture. The paper does not prove it and suggests that a $q$-theoretic or combinatorial proof remains to be found.

333317.title: The cone conjecture for the poset of rational cones
333317.statement:
Let $d$ be a positive integer, and let $\operatorname{Cones}(d)$ denote the poset of rational cones in $\mathbb R^d$, with its order defined by additive generation of lattice points in cones. The inclusion order is the usual order $C\subseteq C'$ for cones $C,C'\subseteq\mathbb R^d$.

**Cone conjecture.** For every $d$, the order in $\operatorname{Cones}(d)$ is the inclusion order.

This is the maximal possible strengthening of the absence of extremal elements in $\operatorname{Cones}(d)$. The paper proves the assertion for $d=3$; the general case remains open in the supplied source.

333321.title: The tope-graph conjecture for finite graphs in $\mathcal{S}_4$
333321.statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}_4$ denote the graph class studied in the paper, and let a **COM** be a complex of oriented matroid covectors; its tope graph is the graph whose vertices are the topes of the COM, with adjacency given by the relevant one-coordinate changes.

**The tope-graph conjecture for finite graphs in $\mathcal{S}_4$.** Every finite graph in $\mathcal{S}_4$ is the tope graph of a COM.

The authors expect this to follow from amalgamation techniques analogous to those used for hypercellular graphs, but the supplied text does not establish it. The precise definition of $\mathcal{S}_4$ and the COM conventions are not included in the supplied context.

333333.title: The first shape-coefficient conjecture for consecutive Dirichlet eigenvalue gaps
333333.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}$ be a bounded domain with piecewise smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$, and let $\lambda_i$ be the $i$-th Dirichlet eigenvalue. Let $\mathfrak{S}_1(\Omega)$ be the first shape coefficient, defined using cubes $\Sigma_1\subset\Omega\subset\Sigma_2$ by the supremum of $d_1^2/d_2^2$ for $n\geq2$, and equal to $1$ for $n=1$. **First shape-coefficient conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$,

$$
\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda_k\leq\mathfrak{S}_1(\Omega)(\lambda_2-\lambda_1)k^{\frac{1}{n}}.
$$

The claim proposes a bound depending only on the first spectral gap and the domain's shape. The paper presents it as motivated by numerical calculations and does not report a general proof.

333334.title: The second shape-coefficient conjecture for consecutive Dirichlet eigenvalue gaps
333334.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}$ be a bounded domain with piecewise smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$, and let $\lambda_i$ be the $i$-th Dirichlet eigenvalue. Let $\mathfrak{S}_2(\Omega)$ be the second shape coefficient, defined using balls $\mathbb{B}_1\subset\Omega\subset\mathbb{B}_2$ by the supremum of $r_1^2/r_2^2$ for $n\geq2$, and equal to $1$ for $n=1$. **Second shape-coefficient conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$,

$$
\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda_k\leq\mathfrak{S}_2(\Omega)(\lambda_2-\lambda_1)k^{\frac{1}{n}}.
$$

This is a companion to the first shape-coefficient claim, replacing enclosing cubes by enclosing balls. It is proposed from numerical evidence, and the source gives no general proof.

333359.title: Obstacle number two conjecture for gyroelongated bipyramids
333359.statement:
Let $X_n$ denote the gyroelongated $n$-bipyramid, and let ${\operatorname{{obs}}}_\mathrm{out}(X_n)$ be its outside obstacle number. **Obstacle-number conjecture.** If $n\geq 4$, then

$$
{\operatorname{{obs}}}_\mathrm{out}(X_n)=2.
$$

The paper establishes this for $n=4,5,6$ and explains that larger cases were not computationally feasible; the conjecture asserts that no representation using only an outside obstacle exists for every larger $n$.

333370.title: The complementary-signature conjecture for weak c-Wilf equivalence
333370.statement: For $k\geq 2$, let $\sigma\in\{+,-\}^k$ be a signature, and define its **complementary signature** $\sigma_c=\sigma_c^0\sigma_c^1\ldots\sigma_c^{k-1}$ by setting $\sigma_c^i=+$ if $\sigma^i=-$ and $\sigma_c^i=-$ if $\sigma^i=+$. **Complementary-signature conjecture.** For all $k\geq 2$ and $\sigma\in\{+,-\}^k$, $\sigma$ is weakly c-Wilf equivalent to $\sigma_c$. This conjecture proposes a general symmetry for cyclic permutation enumeration; its status is unresolved in the supplied source.

333371.title: The alternating-signature conjecture for c-Wilf equivalence
333371.statement: For $k\geq 2$, an **alternating signature of size $k$** is a signature $\sigma$ such that either $\sigma^i=+$ for all even $i$ and $\sigma^i=-$ for all odd $i$, or $\sigma^i=+$ for all odd $i$ and $\sigma^i=-$ for all even $i$. **Alternating-signature conjecture.** For all $k\geq 2$, the alternating signatures of size $k$ are all c-Wilf-equivalent. The source notes that the assertion is automatic for even $k$ by a preceding proposition, leaving the odd-$k$ case as the unresolved part.

333522.title: Jaeger–Linial–Payan–Tarzi additive bases conjecture for finite vector spaces
333522.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $\mathbb{Z}_p^n$ be the $n$-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{Z}_p$, and let an additive basis be a multiset $B$ of elements of $\mathbb{Z}_p^n$ such that

$$
\mathcal{S}(B)=\left\{\sum_{b\in S}b\mid S\subseteq B\right\}=\mathbb{Z}_p^n.
$$

A basis is a basis of the vector space $\mathbb{Z}_p^n$.

**Jaeger–Linial–Payan–Tarzi conjecture.** For every prime $p$, there exists a constant $k_p$ such that the union, with repetitions, of any $k_p$ bases for $\mathbb{Z}_p^n$ forms an additive basis.

This conjecture would generalize important results concerning nowhere-zero flows; in particular, the case $p=3$ would imply the weak $3$-flow conjecture. The source does not provide evidence of a resolution, so the conjecture is recorded as open.

333594.title: Potočnik–Spiga–Verret's semiprimitive graph-restrictiveness conjecture
333594.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite permutation group. Call $G$ **semiprimitive** if every normal subgroup of $G$ is transitive or semiregular, and call $G$ **graph-restrictive** if there is a constant $c(G)$ such that, for every locally $G$ pair $(\Gamma,H)$, the order of a vertex stabiliser in $H$ is at most $c(G)$. **Potočnik–Spiga–Verret's conjecture.**

$$
G\text{ is semiprimitive if and only if }G\text{ is graph-restrictive}.
$$

This is the graph-theoretic problem motivating the paper and is described there as potentially the most intractable problem in the section; the forward implication remains open.

333609.title: The ternary code support 2-design conjecture
333609.statement:
Let $m\geq 3$ be odd, let $v=(3^m-1)/2$, and let $\mathcal{C}_m$ be either of the ternary cyclic codes described in the paper. Let $A_k$ denote the number of codewords of Hamming weight $k$, and define

$$
\mathcal{P}=\{0,1,2,\cdots,v-1\}.
$$

For $A_k\neq 0$, let $\mathcal{B}$ be the set of supports of the weight-$k$ codewords of $\mathcal{C}_m$. **The ternary code support 2-design conjecture.** For every such $k$, $(\mathcal{P},\mathcal{B})$ is a $2$-$(v,k,\lambda)$ design. This predicts that the supports of every nonzero weight in these code families form 2-designs; the paper gives the code constructions and relates the weight-$4$ case to a Steiner-system construction, but the conjecture is not resolved here.

333726.title: The period–extended graph permanent conjecture for 4-point $phi^4$ graphs
333726.statement: Let a **4-point $\phi^4$ graph** be a graph of the type considered in the paper, with period and extended graph permanent as defined there. **Period–extended graph permanent conjecture.** If two 4-point $\phi^4$ graphs have equal periods, then they have equal extended graph permanents. The extended graph permanent is proposed as a non-trivial invariant potentially carrying information about the graph period; the paper proves its invariance under completion/decompletion, Schnetz twists, and planar duality, but equality for all graphs with equal periods remains open.

333908.title: Maximality conjecture for the noncommutative spectral-curve Hamiltonians
333908.statement:
Let $A$ be the free associative algebra of the system, let $[A,A]$ be its commutator subspace, and write the coefficients of the noncommutative spectral curve as

$$
\operatorname{Tr}\,L(\lambda)^k=\sum_{j=-k}^k H_{k,j}\lambda^j.
$$

The induced Lie bracket on $A/[A,A]$ is the one associated with the system. **Spectral-curve maximality conjecture.** The image of $\operatorname{Span}(H_{k,l})$ in $A/[A,A]$ under the natural projection is a maximal commutative Lie subalgebra of $A/[A,A]$ with respect to this induced Lie bracket. The source reports computations showing commutativity for $k,m\leq 5$ and arbitrary indices, but maximality remains conjectural.

334120.title: Conjugation automorphism conjecture for the G-positivity order
334120.statement:
For skew shapes $A$ and $B$, let $A\leq B$ mean that $a_{A,\nu}\leq a_{B,\nu}$ for every partition $\nu$, equivalently that $G_B-G_A$ is $G$ positive. Transposition sends a skew shape $A$ to its transpose $A^T$. **Conjugation automorphism conjecture.** Conjugation acts as an automorphism of this $G$-positivity order: 
$$
A\leq B\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A^T\leq B^T.
$$
 The claim is proposed as an analogue of the corresponding fact for the Schur-positivity order; the source gives no proof or resolution.

334133.title: Bounded stabilization conjecture for plane-curve spectral sequences
334133.statement:
Let $C:f=0$ be any reduced plane curve of degree $d$. For a singular point of $C$, let its Milnor number and Tjurina number be denoted by $bc$ and $c$ respectively; write $bc(C)$ and $c(C)$ for their totals. For integers $t$ and $k$, set $q=td+k$.

**Bounded stabilization conjecture.** There is a positive integer $q_0\leq 3d+1$ such that

$$
\dim E_2^{1-t,t}(f)_k=\mu(C)-\tau(C)\quad\text{and}\quad E_3^{1-t,t}(f)_k=0
$$

for every $q=td+k\geq q_0$. The minimal positive integer with this property, if it exists, is denoted by $q_0(f)$.

This more precise form of the preceding conjectural claims is proposed to speed up computations. The source does not provide a proof or a resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
